title: Research
text:
Research Experience

Stanford University — The Rural Education Action Program (REAP) · Wuhan, China
Research Assistant · Aug. 2025 – Present
I conduct empirical analysis in Stata and R across four early-childhood-development RCTs, applying balance tests, attrition analyses, Lee Bounds, and subgroup-level heterogeneous treatment effects with Romano-Wolf correction. In the field, I led a household survey in rural Hubei with sample coverage grown from 600 to 856, built real-time dashboards across 105 villages, and assisted my supervisor in distributing LENA devices to 467 families.


Honors Thesis Program, University of California, Davis
Honors Thesis Student · Aug. 2024 – Jan. 2025
Completed an honors thesis evaluating farmers’ responses to alternative agricultural insurance contracts, finding that discount-based insurance raised input expenditures by 35–40% relative to rebates. Estimated treatment effects with ANCOVA, IV regression, and farmer fixed effects, and presented at the UC Davis Undergraduate Research Conference and the 2025 AIARD Annual Conference.


Agroecology, Gaudin Lab, University of California, Davis
Research Assistant · Jun. 2024 – Sept. 2024
Screened and extracted data from 78 of 260 studies on agricultural practices in drought-prone areas, contributing to a meta-analysis on drought-resistance strategies for smallholder farmers.


Sustainability, Community, and Technology in Nepal · Pokhara, Nepal
Project Member · Sept. 2023 – Jan. 2024
Joined a 40-member cross-cultural team to collect household data from 15 dairy farming families in rural Nepal, and produced a consulting plan covering financial analysis, equipment financing, and government grants.

title: Zheng (Quinn) Wang
text:
About
I am an applied economics researcher working at the intersection of agricultural and development economics. My research focuses on technology adoption and adaptation in rural, resource-limited regions. I am currently a Research Assistant at Stanford University’s Rural Education Action Program (REAP), where my work also spans early childhood development and gender inequality.
